samf-junior-2020-r2-02.title: Find the next square
samf-junior-2020-r2-02.body:
$44^2=1936$ and $45^2=2025$, so the next square year is $2025$, which is in $5$ years' time.

**Answer: 5**

samf-junior-2020-r2-03.title: Fraction of the circle
samf-junior-2020-r2-03.body:
The shaded sector lies between the horizontal radius (marked as perpendicular to the vertical line) and a radius at half of the right angle, i.e. it is a $45^\circ$ sector, which is $\frac18$ of the circle. $\frac18\times160=20$.

**Answer: 20**

samf-junior-2020-r2-04.title: Isosceles triangles
samf-junior-2020-r2-04.body:
The left triangle has base angle $20^\circ$ at the left corner and its two sides along the base and the inner left side are equal, so its angle at the top (left part) is also $20^\circ$ and its angle at the inner base point is $140^\circ$. The angle of the middle triangle at that point is $180-140=40^\circ$. The middle triangle is isosceles with equal base angles $40^\circ$, so its apex angle is $x=180-2\times40=100$.

**Answer: 100**

samf-junior-2020-r2-04.title: Angle sum of the left half
samf-junior-2020-r2-04.body:
Around the top vertex the angles are $20^\circ$, $x$ and $20^\circ$ (the outer triangles' apex angles). Adding the four $20^\circ$ angles that appear at the base and apex of the isosceles side triangles gives $20\times4+x=180$, so $x=100$.

**Answer: 100**

samf-junior-2020-r2-05.title: Count squares
samf-junior-2020-r2-05.body:
The staircase has rows of $1,2,\dots,9$ squares: $45$ squares in total. $20\%$ of $45$ is $9$. There are $7$ black squares already, so $2$ more are needed.

**Answer: 2**

samf-junior-2020-r2-07.title: Per second
samf-junior-2020-r2-07.body:
$50$ revolutions per $60$ seconds is $\frac56$ of a revolution per second, which is $\frac56\times360^\circ=300^\circ$.

**Answer: 300**

samf-junior-2020-r2-08.title: Twice a triangle
samf-junior-2020-r2-08.body:
Reflection in $AQ$ maps triangle $ADQ$ onto triangle $AD'Q$, so $ADQD'$ has twice the area of triangle $ADQ$. Triangle $ADQ$ has a right angle at $D$ with legs $AD=4$ and $DQ=2$: area $\frac12\cdot4\cdot2=4$. So the quadrilateral has area $8$.

**Answer: 8**

samf-junior-2020-r2-09.title: Count
samf-junior-2020-r2-09.body:
The single A is in the first or second position ($2$ ways), the other letter is B, C or D ($3$ ways), and the number is $1$ or $3$ ($2$ ways): $2\times3\times2=12$.

**Answer: 12**

samf-junior-2020-r2-10.title: List the squares
samf-junior-2020-r2-10.body:
The two-digit perfect squares are $16,25,36,49,64,81$. For $\overline{abc}$ we need $\overline{ab}$ and $\overline{bc}$ both in this list, so the second digit of the first square is the first digit of the second. Chains: $16\to64$ ($164$), $36\to64$ ($364$), $64\to49$ ($649$), $81\to16$ ($816$). $25$ would need a square starting with $5$, $49$ with $9$: none beyond those. The largest is $816$.

**Answer: 816**

samf-junior-2020-r2-11.title: Count small triangles
samf-junior-2020-r2-11.body:
The diagram can be subdivided into $22$ identical equilateral triangles (each hexagon is $6$, the overlaps are accounted for by the picture). So each has area $176\div22=8$ and the four shaded triangles have area $4\times8=32$.

**Answer: 32**

samf-junior-2020-r2-12.title: Two equations
samf-junior-2020-r2-12.body:
Let the sides be $x$ and $y$. Three sides total either $2x+y$ or $x+2y$, so $2x+y=73$ and $x+2y=77$. Adding: $3x+3y=150$, so $x+y=50$ and the perimeter is $2(x+y)=100$.

**Answer: 100**

samf-junior-2020-r2-13.title: Pythagoras
samf-junior-2020-r2-13.body:
Let the legs be $x$ and $3x$: $x^2+9x^2=400$, so $x^2=40$. The area is $\frac12\cdot x\cdot3x=\frac32x^2=60$.

**Answer: 60**

samf-junior-2020-r2-14.title: Chase angles
samf-junior-2020-r2-14.body:
Since $\triangle DEC$ is equilateral, $\angle DCE=60^\circ$ and $\angle ECB=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$. Also $CE=CD=CB$, so $\triangle ECB$ is isosceles with apex $30^\circ$ and $\angle EBC=\angle CEB=75^\circ$. As $EB=EF$, triangle $BEF$ is isosceles and $\angle EFB=\angle EBF=75^\circ$, so $\angle EFC=105^\circ$. In triangle $CEF$: $\angle CEF=180-30-105=45^\circ$.

**Answer: 45**

samf-junior-2020-r2-15.title: Place the two 5s
samf-junior-2020-r2-15.body:
The typed number is $2020$ with two $5$s inserted. Choose which two of the $6$ positions hold the $5$s: $\binom62=15$. Each gives a different $6$-digit number (none starts with $0$).

**Answer: 15**

samf-junior-2020-r2-15.title: Count insertions
samf-junior-2020-r2-15.body:
The first $5$ can be inserted in $5$ places and the second in $6$; this counts every number twice (the $5$s are identical): $\frac{5\times6}2=15$.

**Answer: 15**

samf-junior-2020-r2-17.title: Compare lost and gained surface
samf-junior-2020-r2-17.body:
Every piece of surface that is cut away from the original (from the front and from the top) is replaced by an inner face of the same area, so these cancel out. The only new surface is the pair of end faces of the removed block, each $3\times2=6\text{ cm}^2$, which face each other inside the cut. So the surface area is $96+6+6=108\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: 108**

samf-junior-2020-r2-18.title: Simplest fraction
samf-junior-2020-r2-18.body:
$96.8\%=\frac{968}{1000}=\frac{121}{125}$ in simplest form. So the number of pupils is a multiple of $125$, and the smallest group has $125$ pupils with $121$ passing, so $4$ did not pass.

**Answer: 4**

samf-junior-2020-r2-19.title: Triangle ABC is isosceles
samf-junior-2020-r2-19.body:
$\angle ABC=\angle ACB=180^\circ-x$, so triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with equal base angles at $B$ and $C$. The angle $48^\circ$ and the angle $y$ can be: (i) the two base angles are $48^\circ$ each and $\angle BAC=y=180-96=84$; (ii) $\angle BAC=48^\circ$ and the base angles are $y$: $y=\frac{180-48}2=66$; (iii) one base angle is $48^\circ$ and the other base angle is $y$, so $y=48$. The sum is $84+66+48=198$.

**Answer: 198**

samf-junior-2020-r2-20.title: Equation
samf-junior-2020-r2-20.body:
Let there be $x$ pupils: $\frac23x$ boys. Afterwards there are $x+1$ pupils and the boys are $\frac35(x+1)$. So $\frac23x-1=\frac35(x+1)$, giving $10x-15=9x+9$ and $x=24$.

**Answer: 24**

samf-junior-2020-r2-20.title: Multiples
samf-junior-2020-r2-20.body:
Originally pupils $=3k$ ($2k$ boys, $k$ girls); afterwards $2k-1$ boys and $k+2$ girls in ratio $3:2$: $2(2k-1)=3(k+2)$, so $k=8$ and the class had $24$ pupils.

**Answer: 24**

samf-junior-2020-r2-21.title: Translate to form a right triangle
samf-junior-2020-r2-21.body:
Translate $AB$ to $EC$ (so that $E$ lies on the line through $C$ parallel to $AB$) and $BC$ to $AE$. Then $AE=8$ and $ED=EC+CD=6+9=15$, with a right angle at $E$. So $AD=\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=17$ cm.

**Answer: 17**

samf-junior-2020-r2-22.title: Chain the speeds
samf-junior-2020-r2-22.body:
Vlad gains $25$ m on Hagrid every $250$ m, so when Vlad has run $1000$ m Hagrid has run $900$ m. Hagrid gains $20$ m on Sanjev per $500$ m, so by $900$ m Hagrid is $\frac{900}{500}\times20=36$ m ahead of Sanjev, i.e. Sanjev has run $864$ m. Sanjev is $1000-864=136$ m behind Vlad.

**Answer: 136**

samf-junior-2020-r2-22.title: Speed ratios
samf-junior-2020-r2-22.body:
Hagrid : Vlad $=225:250=9:10$; Sanjev : Hagrid $=480:500=24:25$. Sanjev : Vlad $=\frac9{10}\cdot\frac{24}{25}=\frac{216}{250}$, so when Vlad has run $1000$ Sanjev has run $864$ m: $136$ m behind.

**Answer: 136**

samf-junior-2020-r2-23.title: Two equations
samf-junior-2020-r2-23.body:
Let the table, cat and dog have heights $T$, $C$, $D$. The first picture gives $T+D-C=180$ and the second gives $T+C-D=140$. Adding: $2T=320$, so $T=160$ cm.

**Answer: 160**

samf-junior-2020-r2-24.title: Side lengths and slopes
samf-junior-2020-r2-24.body:
The squares have sides $2$, $6$ and $3$. Along $AB$, the top corners of the squares of side $2$ and $6$ lie on $AB$, a rise of $4$ over a horizontal distance of $2$ (the width of the small square), so $AB$ has slope $2$ and meets the base $1$ cm to the left of the small square. Along $AC$, the top corners of the squares of side $6$ and $3$ are $3$ cm higher and $3$ cm apart horizontally, so slope $1$, and $AC$ meets the base $3$ cm to the right of the square of side $3$. Therefore $BC=1+2+6+3+3=15$.

**Answer: 15**

samf-junior-2020-r2-25.title: Half-turn about the midpoint of BD
samf-junior-2020-r2-25.body:
Let $\triangle BCD$ be rotated through $180^\circ$ about the midpoint of $BD$; $B$ and $D$ swap and $C$ goes to $C'$. Then $\angle BDC'=\angle DBC=125^\circ$ and $\angle ADB=55^\circ$, so $A$, $D$, $C'$ are collinear. Also $\angle DBC'=\angle BDC=10^\circ$, so $\angle ABC'=35^\circ+10^\circ=45^\circ$. Triangle $ABC'$ has a right angle at $A$ and a $45^\circ$ angle at $B$, so it is right isosceles with $AC'=AB=20$. Its area $\frac12\cdot20\cdot20=200$ equals the area of $ABCD$ (triangle $ABD$ plus the rotated copy of triangle $BCD$).

**Answer: 200**

samf-junior-2020-r2-25.title: Trigonometry check
samf-junior-2020-r2-25.body:
$AD=20\tan35^\circ\approx14.0$, $BD=20/\cos35^\circ\approx24.4$, and by the sine rule in $BCD$, $BC=BD\sin10^\circ/\sin45^\circ\approx6.0$. Then $[ABD]\approx140.0$ and $[BCD]=\frac12\,BC\cdot BD\sin125^\circ\approx60.0$, total $\approx200$.

**Answer: 200**
